source.title: Learning Shrinks the Hard Tail: Training-Dependent Inference Scaling in a Solvable Linear Model

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper extends scaling-law analysis to a solvable linear fine-tuning setting and reports results on CIFAR-10H and a GSM8K distillation task. It does not test language-model pretraining scaling in parameters, tokens, or compute.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own generalization-loss results as training sample size varies in a linear model, CIFAR-10H linear-head fine-tuning, and GSM8K teacher–student distillation. Those results bear on V5 and, for the linear model’s regime changes, V7. It does not measure held-out pretraining cross-entropy over language-model size, tokens, or compute, test small-run prediction of larger pretraining runs, or test a parameter–token compute-optimal split. Its pass@k results concern inference scaling, not a measure named by the claim versions.
record.test_reason: The study's own experiments measure held-out loss against fine-tuning sample size in two fine-tuning settings: a frozen ResNet-18 with a linear head on CIFAR-10H, and LoRA distillation of Flan-T5-small on GSM8K. These bear only weakly on V5's fine-tuning regime. The linear-model results (R1–R3) re-derive known ridge/OLS theory on synthetic features rather than test a trained model. The paper's main subject, pass@k inference scaling, is not a measure named by any version.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that generalization loss follows established sample-size scaling in the LID linear model. Their main claim is that the pass@k exponent βeff(N) grows with N and saturates at β, which implies investing in training before saturation and in inference attempts after. They present CIFAR-10H and GSM8K as real-data proxies showing analogous behaviour.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a solvable linear last-layer regression model with stochastic, instance-dependent targets, plus CIFAR-10H feature fitting and GSM8K teacher–student distillation. It does not reproduce language-model pretraining sweeps over parameter count, tokens, or compute.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper states that the overparameterized and underparameterized exponents differ by regime and that the double-descent peak depends on regularization and the feature spectrum. It also notes that the empirical inference fit depends weakly on the k-window and estimator, and that GSM8K saturation depends on LoRA capacity and teacher/student choice.

fits_no_version.finding: In the synthetic LID linear ridge model, generalization loss scales as N^-α for N<d and as d/N for N≫d, with a double-descent peak at N≈d. Simulations (Fig. 1 left) confirm this.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sample-size learning curves of linear last-layer regression follow regime-dependent power laws set by the feature spectrum and noise.

fits_no_version.finding: The pass@k failure exponent βeff(N) rises with training-set size and saturates at an intrinsic difficulty index β. This is shown in simulation, CIFAR-10H (plateau about 0.27) and GSM8K.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Inference-time pass@k scaling exponents depend on training progress and saturate.

record.problems: The theoretical analysis is for a linear last-layer model and does not establish language-model pretraining scaling. The empirical tests are limited to CIFAR-10H frozen features and one small GSM8K distillation setup. The GSM8K test-loss proxy is described as unstable, and valid-parse coverage is not plotted. No uncertainty estimates are stated.
record.rows_left_out: No separate generalization-loss result bearing on V5 or V7 was left out. Pass@k and compute-allocation results were not recorded as rows because the claim versions do not name those measures or the training-sample/inference-attempt allocation studied here.

untested.parts: No pretraining loss sweep over parameters, tokens or compute.
No extrapolation from small to large runs.
No parameter–token compute-optimal split; the paper's allocation is between training samples and inference attempts.
Only sample-size scaling in two small fine-tuning setups is tested; no model-size scaling, video or image generative models, repeated data, or transfer scaling.
No downstream performance against scale or pretraining loss; pass@k is varied over attempts, not model scale.
No test of fitting choices, parameter counting, schedules, or disagreement between published laws.

record.verdict_notes: The bearing on the scaling-law claim is marginal. The only V5-relevant evidence is qualitative sample-size curves in two small fine-tuning setups, with no reported exponents, fits or uncertainties. The paper's novel content (pass@k exponent coupling) falls outside all versions. The linear-theory rows are re-derivations of cited results and should not count as tests.

versions.untested_parts: No language-model pretraining cross-entropy sweep over parameters, tokens, or compute.
No test of predictions from small language-model pretraining runs against substantially larger runs.
The paper studies allocation between training samples and inference attempts, not the loss-minimizing parameter and token counts at fixed training compute.
No controlled comparison of depth, width, or other architectures at fixed parameter count.

The experiments cover linear last-layer fine-tuning on image features and one small teacher–student distillation task; they do not test video models, repeated-data regimes, transfer scaling, or whether the same laws hold broadly across modalities and training regimes.
No test of downstream-task performance scaling as a function of pretraining loss or scale.

The paper does not test language-model pretraining fit choices, parameter-counting conventions, disagreements between the cited language-model laws, or how those choices change the parameter–token compute-optimal split.

rows.measure: Generalization loss against the mean target

rows.note: The paper describes distinct scaling regimes on either side of the interpolation region, rather than one power law covering the transition.

rows.subject: frozen ResNet-18 + linear head
rows.stage_stated: pretrained image backbone frozen; linear head fine-tuned
rows.operation_detail: Fits the linear head on varying numbers of CIFAR-10H examples and measures held-out generalization loss.
rows.measure: MSE generalization loss against the rescaled human mean label
rows.value: The curve has a transition near N ≈ d and a 1/N decay for N ≫ d.
rows.note: Human label variance is treated as instance-dependent noise; the paper describes the observed scaling qualitatively.
rows.check: The result is qualitative only: no fitted exponent or uncertainty is reported. The 1/N tail holds for N≫d, with a transition near N≈d=512. Baseline is an N^-1 reference line, not a control.

rows.subject: Flan-T5-small (LoRA student)
rows.stage_stated: fine-tuned by distillation from Flan-T5-XL; one epoch
rows.operation_detail: Fine-tunes on increasing subsets of GSM8K training examples and measures a strict greedy valid-only MSE proxy.
rows.measure: Strict greedy valid-only test MSE proxy
rows.value: The loss decreases modestly with N; the paper says the test loss is unstable due to large numerical mismatches, though its overall trend decreases.
rows.note: The text does not establish that this metric follows the N^-1 reference; valid-parse coverage is tracked but not plotted.
rows.check: The loss decreases only modestly and the authors call it unstable. No fit to the N^-1 reference is shown, and valid-parse coverage is not plotted.
